sources.entry: bandersnatch - PyPI mirroring tool provided by the Python Packaging Authority (PyPA).

summary.one_liner: bandersnatch is a PyPI mirroring client from the Python Packaging Authority that syncs PyPI's static package files and metadata to a local mirror.
summary.what_it_does: Implements PEP 381, PEP 503, and PEP 691 mirroring of the Python Package Index. It uses the PEP 691 Simple JSON API for package metadata and, since version 8.0, mirrors PEP 658 / PEP 714 core metadata files (on by default via the core-metadata config option). The mirror is served as static files from the web/ subdirectory, which a webserver such as nginx can publish. Commands include mirror, delete, and verify, plus a --force-check flag for a full resync. Blocklist and allowlist plugins limit which packages are mirrored. A runner script in the Docker image runs mirror periodically.
use_cases: mirror PyPI locally for an organization
reduce WAN bandwidth for pip installs
serve Python packages on an internal network
limit a local mirror to selected packages with an allowlist or blocklist
run periodic PyPI syncs from cron or systemd timers
stack: PEP 381 / PEP 503 / PEP 691 / PEP 658 / PEP 714 mirroring protocols
notable: Mirrors PEP 691 Simple JSON API metadata and PEP 658 / PEP 714 core metadata files
Plugin-based blocklist and allowlist to reduce mirror size
Official Docker image with a runner script for periodic mirroring
Maintained under the Python Packaging Authority (PyPA)
caveats: Requires a case-sensitive filesystem and a filesystem that handles many subdirectories (ext4 or newer recommended, ext3 avoided)
On Windows it needs an elevated prompt or symlink permissions
Mirror lags PyPI by up to about an hour due to CDN caching; full syncs can take hours. The README also asks for more maintainers.
